problem: The caption says "the kernel schedules hardware". The scheduler schedules processes (tasks), not hardware; the kernel drives or controls hardware through drivers. As written, a student can form the wrong idea of what the scheduler does, and it contradicts Section 2, which correctly says the scheduler gives turns to processes.
fix: Caption: Three logged-in users reach one kernel through their shells; the kernel schedules their processes on the CPU, drives the hardware through drivers, and can load a module.

problem: "or a higher-priority event arrives" is vague. Preemption happens when a higher-priority task becomes runnable or when the running task blocks or its time slice ends. "Event" hides the key point, which is a task becoming ready.
fix: "When the slice ends, or when a higher-priority process becomes ready to run, the kernel preempts the running process and switches to another."

problem: The lead lists "Android phones" as an example of a machine that "must serve many users". A phone normally has a single user account; multi-user login is the shared-server and cloud case, not the everyday phone case. The example slightly muddles the feature being introduced.
fix: "These features make Linux common on shared lab servers and cloud machines, where one machine serves many users at once, and the same kernel sits inside every Android phone."
